newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Gidusa sees '97 sales up 12 pct vs '96.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Gidusa sees '97 sales up 12 pct vs '96.

text.p: Mexican paper and packaging company Grupo Industrial Durango (Gidusa) expects 1997 sales to rise 12 percent over the $375 million recorded last year, Jose Antonio Rincon, the company's executive vice-president, said at a media conference.
"We are talking about a (sales) growth rate of 12 percent over 1996, which ended at $375 million," Rincon said.
Rincon added that Gidusa plans to invest $18 million in 1997 in machinery for the company's 35 plants around the country, which he said would boost both production output and sales.
Gidusa, he added, was also mulling plans to construct plants in the United States along the border with Mexico.
"We are working with our development team looking for areas of opportunity for growth outside the country, but above all in areas close to the border," Rincon added.
